title: Broadleaf, Rough + Bunker Surrounds, Knapsack
sheet_name: Milwaukee 15L 450L/Ha - Rough + Bunker Surrounds/Tongues - Broadleaf (19 Nov)
fill_how: Fill to the 10 L mark with clean water
No agitator on a knapsack: lid on and swirl the tank after each product
Rinse the measuring jug into the tank as you go
checks: Tank, hose and wand rinsed since the last job
Residue from the last mix can damage this one
Tank strainer and wand filter clean, lid seal good
Wand, trigger and nozzle work, no drips or leaks at the hose
One tank should cover about 18 × 18 m at a steady walk. Emptying it over less ground is too heavy
Wash water, eyewash and spill kit on the cart
Labels and SDSs for all 5 products at the shed
Spray signs out where you're working
Wind 3–20 km/h (Tri-Kombi label). Today: not before about 10am, once the dew is off and the breeze is up
extra_checks: Stop the spray short of the bent. No drift onto putting surfaces

how: Pour into the water, lid on, swirl

products.why: Soluble amine salts go in after the buffer. You're at {before} L.
The second amine-salt hormone. You're at {before} L.

products.note: Dye goes in 4th (sheet has it 5th), before the Hasten.

how: Lid on tight and swirl well. Swirl again each time you pick the tank back up

ppe_note: Tri-Kombi's label asks for a half-face respirator with organic vapour cartridges, elbow gloves and chemical-resistant clothing buttoned at the neck and wrist when mixing and when spraying by hand. Goggles when pouring.
spray_rules: Broadleaf weeds on bunker tongues, surrounds and rough only. One light, even pass until the dye shows, not to run-off
Stay off greens and collars. Stop the spray short of the bent and keep the wand low
Not before about 10am: wait for the dew to dry and the breeze to pick up. Wind 3–20 km/h. Stop when it gusts toward a green, tee or garden bed
Stay out from under tree drip lines and away from garden beds
Keep golfers off until it's dry. Write down where you sprayed: no mowing there for 2 days
spray_more: Tri-Kombi label: wind 3–20 km/h, no spraying in a surface inversion (calm, dewy mornings), don't mow 2 days before or after, don't irrigate to run-off for 3 days. One tank is about 330 m²: if it empties over less ground it's going on too heavy.
post_checks: Tank sprayed out on the target area
Tank, hose and wand flushed with clean water
Rinse water sprayed back over the rough you treated
Not down a drain or onto hard surfaces
Suit, gloves and goggles washed. Respirator wiped, cartridges sealed in a bag
So the mowing (not before Sat 21 Nov) can skip them
post_fields: e.g. tongues and surrounds 17, 18, 8, 9 · clover at the 6th tee

flags.t: Tri-Kombi label: not by backpack sprayer
flags.d: Restraint on the current label: DO NOT apply by spraying equipment carried on the back of the user. This tank goes out through the Milwaukee knapsacks. For hand-held spraying the label asks for chemical-resistant clothing, elbow gloves and a half-face respirator. Flagged to Andy 19 Nov.

flags.t: Tri-Kombi label: no heavy rain or storms within 3 days
flags.d: Restraint: DO NOT apply if heavy rains or storms are forecast within 3 days. This morning's brief has about 20 mm for Friday 20 Nov. The label also says don't irrigate to run-off for 3 days. Flagged to Andy 19 Nov.

flags.t: Methar Tri-Kombi 4.5 L/ha is over its label maximum
flags.d: The label sets 4.2 L/ha as the maximum (its greens and lawns row still reads 45 mL per 100 m², which is 4.5 L/ha). This tank has 150 mL; at the label max it would be 140 mL. Victoria allows off-label use at or below the label rate, not above it. Built as the sheet stands (Andy, 19 Nov: normal rates).

flags.t: Sportsground + Tri-Kombi: the same three-way twice
flags.d: Both are Campbell three-ways with mecoprop 336 + dicamba 40 g/L. At 4.5 L/ha each that's about 3.0 kg/ha mecoprop and 360 g/ha dicamba, against 1.4 kg/ha and 168 g/ha at Tri-Kombi's label maximum. Same loading as the 19 Oct handgun tank on the rough. The page keeps the crew off greens and collars.

APVMA 31538. The eLabel is a scan with no readable text and GreenKeeper's label link is dead. Campbell's catalogue lists mecoprop 336 + MCPA 80 + dicamba 40 g/L. PPE on this page follows the Tri-Kombi label. Check the drum for its rate and for any backpack restraint.

flags.t: Hasten isn't on the Tri-Kombi label
flags.d: The label doesn't call for an oil adjuvant. Oil with hormone herbicides bites harder in heat: 28 °C forecast, warm from 1pm.

Sheet is 450 L/ha, the Tri-Kombi label water rate. Andy: setting 3 on these knapsacks typically puts out about 400 L/ha, 450 kept. At 400 L/ha a tank covers about 375 m² and the rates land about 11% under the sheet.
Hasten's label says add it last, so Tru Blue goes in 4th and Hasten 5th. Rates are as the sheet.

6th station 4:50am: 13.4 °C, RH 96%, calm, Delta T 0.7, heavy dew. Brief has Delta T under 2 until about 10am, 3–6 from 11am with 4–8 km/h, gusts to about 22 late morning, 28 °C. Label wind is 3–20 km/h with no spraying in an inversion, so not before about 10am.
Tri-Kombi: don't mow 2 days before or after, don't irrigate to run-off for 3 days. The post-application checklist asks for the areas sprayed so the mowing can skip them.
